messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired PD#78921 — service=redis-prod-main — symptom=maxclients_reached — region=us-west-2 — severity=high
Alex Chen: acked. I'm on it. seeing a sharp connection spike from a few hosts.
Priya Nair: oncall logging in, any recent deploys or cron jobs?
Alex Chen: no deploys in last hour. running quick check: `redis-cli -h redis-prod-main -p 6379 INFO clients` -> `connected_clients: 10496` `maxclients: 10000` and logs show "ERR max number of clients reached" repeatedly.
Marco Ruiz: embedding service (emb-v2) is returning 503s and high tail latency. dashboards show error rate ~1.8% overall, but spiking on embedding routes.
Alex Chen: TL;DR: redis hit maxclients, clients piled up. root looks like a background batch + misbehaving worker pool. immediate mitigation: `redis-cli CONFIG SET maxclients 20000` (temp) — this lets more connections in while we reduce client count. applied.
PagerDuty: Escalation timer set: 10m to ops-lead if not resolved.
Priya Nair: good call. can we also reduce pressure from the bulk job? who's owning the batch?
Marco Ruiz: that job is from `ingest-worker-03` group, they recently ramped concurrency. I'll pause the scheduled job: `airflow pause ingest_daily_batch` and reduce concurrency to 4.
Alex Chen: pausing batch now. also temporarily flipped a safety flag in gateway to avoid prefetching embeddings: `kubectl -n platform set env deploy/gateway DISABLE_EMBEDDING_PREFETCH=true` — should reduce concurrent client spikes from frontend.
Alex Chen: monitoring `connected_clients` after actions...
incident-bot: system note: logs show repeated lines: `ERR max number of clients reached` from 176.34.22.11 (ingest-worker-03).
Alex Chen: after config change + pausing job, connected_clients dropped from 10496 -> 4200 in ~90s. error rate on emb endpoints falling.
Priya Nair: nice. do we need a short-term connection throttle at the load balancer? we can add a rate limit for the ingress for the ingest worker subnet.
Alex Chen: applied a temporary ip-based limit: `kubectl exec -n infra iptables -A FORWARD -s 176.34.22.0/24 -m connlimit --connlimit-above 200 -j REJECT` — stops the worst offenders.
pagerbot: note: CONFIG SET is not persistent across redis restarts. recommend making the change in the ansible role or redis config template.
Alex Chen: filing a follow-up PR to persist `maxclients: 20000` to infra repo, will link. also creating alert rule: `redis.maxclients > 80% for 5m` to give earlier warning.
Marco Ruiz: customer impact: we saw ~2% request failures on generation/embedding routes for ~12m. CS is tracking a couple of affected accounts; not widespread but nontrivial.
Priya Nair: tagging incident visibility: impacted customers list going to SRE-incident channel and CS. I'll coordinate.
Alex Chen: handoff notes for next rotation (Priya): root cause suspected: background batch ramp + client pool misconfiguration in embedding workers -> leaked/long-lived connections -> redis exhausted maxclients. Actions done: CONFIG SET maxclients=20000 (temp), paused ingest job, flipped prefetch FF, applied ip connlimit, added alert, will persist config and add per-client quotas.
Priya Nair: taking over monitoring for the next 30m. I'll watch health and coordinate follow-ups. please paste the PR/issue links here when created. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: PagerDuty: PD#78921 acknowledged by Alex Chen. Next: escalate to ops-lead if no update by 1769532700.
Alex Chen: created infra PR: https://git.company/infra/merge_requests/4321 — adds persistent maxclients and documents the runbook. created incident ticket INC-5642 for postmortem.
Priya Nair: thanks. I'll draft the impact note for CS and ops. handoff complete. :rotating_light:
